news.title: Ghana, South Africa end WAFCON with wins to keep Women's World Cup qualification hopes alive
news.lede: South Africa and Ghana clinched Africa’s two spots in an intercontinental playoff to qualify for the Women’s World Cup with wins over Nigeria and Ivory Coast. Nigeria’s 2-1 loss to South Africa means the Super Falcons will miss the World Cup for the first time since the tournament’s inauguration in 1991. Ghana came from behind to beat Ivory Coast 2-1 earlier as the four beaten quarterfinalists at the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations were pitted against each other to decide which two progress to the World Cup intercontinental playoffs. The four semifinalists – Cameroon, Malawi, Morocco and Algeria – have all qualified directly for next year’s tournament in Brazil.

news.title: Women's World Cup 2027: Nigeria miss out as South Africa and Ghana win African play-offs
news.lede: Thembi Kgatlana scored two goals at the 2023 Women's World Cup and netted again in Casablanca to keep alive South Africa's hopes of returning to the tournament. Nigeria have failed to qualify for the Fifa Women's World Cup for the first time after they were beaten 2-1 by South Africa in a play-off at the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon). The continent's top-ranked team went into the tournament in Morocco as favourites to retain their title but were eliminated in the quarter-finals by Cameroon, having already lost to Malawi in the group stage. With the four semi-finalists guaranteed a spot at next year's World Cup, Justin Madugu's side had one more chance to keep alive their hopes of reaching Brazil, with the winner of their one-off tie in Casablanca entering an inter-confederation qualifier.

news.title: Banyana Banyana end Nigeria’s World Cup streak with play-in victory
news.lede: But for Nigeria’s Super Falcons, it is the end of the road as they fail to qualify for the World Cup for the first time in their history following a disastrous campaign at the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations, where they also failed to reach the semi-finals for the first time. It will no doubt spark plenty of soul-searching in the West African nation, whose men also failed to qualify for the 2026 World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada. South Africa have been below par at WAFCON themselves as they exited in the quarter-finals, but saved their best performance for last. The first half was devoid of clear-cut chances for either side, though Nigeria’s Michelle Alozie skewed her shot wide when well placed on the edge of the box.

news.title: ‘This was my World Cup’ says Somali ref after Uefa Super Cup
news.lede: Referee Omar Artan reacts during the Uefa Super Cup match between Paris St-Germain and Aston Villa in Salzburg, Austria. (EPA Images pic) PARIS: Somali referee Omar Artan described taking charge of Wednesday's Uefa Super Cup between Paris St-Germain and Aston Villa in Salzburg as his "World Cup". The 34-year-old was denied the chance to referee at the World Cup itself after being refused entry to the United States. He was turned away on arrival at Miami International Airport, despite being part of the panel of referees selected by FIFA for the tournament.

news.title: Ghana fight back to beat Côte d’Ivoire and keep World Cup dream alive
news.lede: Ghana came from behind to defeat Côte d’Ivoire 2-1 and secure a place in the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 inter-confederation play-offs after a dramatic TotalEnergies CAF Women’s Africa Cup of Nations play-off in Casablanca. The Black Queens trailed after just four minutes at the Larbi Zaouli Stadium when Ines Konan converted a penalty to give Côte d’Ivoire the perfect start. But Ghana produced a determined second-half response, with Princess Marfo equalising in the 59th minute before Josephine Bonsu scored from the penalty spot in the 72nd minute to complete the turnaround. The result keeps alive Ghana’s hopes of returning to the Women’s World Cup for the first time since 2007 and gives the Black Queens another route towards qualification for Brazil 2027.

news.title: Rodri transfer news: Man City reject £55m bid from Barcelona for World Cup-winning midfielder
news.lede: Manchester City have rejected a new £55m bid from Barcelona for Rodri. Last week Barcelona had an initial offer in the region of £40m knocked back . On Wednesday, Sky Sports News reported that Barca were expected to raise their offer to between £50m and £60m, but their new offer is still not enough for City. Barcelona remain determined to sign Rodri and are considering their next move.

news.title: Nigeria fail to qualify for Women’s World Cup for first time after South Africa defeat
news.lede: Nigeria, who have competed in every World Cup since the tournament's formation in 1991, are 10-time and reigning WAFCON champions.
